articles.title: Short-term SSRI use alters brain connectivity in anxious individuals in unexpected ways
articles.summary: A new brain imaging study reveals that short-term use of the antidepressant escitalopram actually increases connectivity between key emotion-processing brain regions in anxious individuals, contradicting previous theories about how these drugs physically relieve anxiety.

articles.title: Too much or too little sleep may make your body age faster
articles.summary: Both too little and too much sleep may be linked to faster aging throughout the body. Researchers analyzing 23 biological aging clocks found the lowest aging levels among people sleeping about 6.4 to 7.8 hours per day. Short or long sleep was also associated with numerous conditions affecting the brain, heart, lungs, metabolism, and digestive system.

articles.title: The gender gap in politics is not widening as much as you think
articles.summary: Despite narratives of a growing political divide between the sexes, new research shows that men and women actually shift their opinions in parallel. Major national events, rather than generational changes, drive these unified shifts in public opinion.

articles.title: How family accommodation impacts anxiety and OCD treatment across the lifespan
articles.summary: When family members help loved ones avoid anxiety triggers, it can accidentally worsen symptoms. New research shows that while this behavior is common across all ages, specialized treatment can successfully reverse its effects and lead to recovery.

articles.title: How the stories we tell about ourselves reveal hidden personality disorders
articles.summary: How people construct the stories of their lives offers insight into the severity of their personality disorders. Researchers found that narrating life events with a focus on negative self-change strongly predicted everyday functional impairment.

articles.title: Donald Trump’s New York accent has subtly shifted over the past five decades
articles.summary: Acoustic analysis of Donald Trump’s speech from 1980 to 2023 reveals that while he largely maintained his classic New York accent, he steadily shifted his pronunciation of stigmatized vowels.

articles.title: Researchers followed 400,000 kids for 20 years and found a lasting pre-K advantage
articles.summary: A 20-year study of 400,000 students found that children who attended public school pre-K earned better grades and test scores through high school than those in other childcare settings. Better-trained teachers and earlier exposure to structured classrooms may help explain why the advantage lasted so long.

articles.title: Smart nanoparticles light up brain cancer and destroy what surgery misses
articles.summary: Scientists created smart nanoparticles that can both illuminate hidden glioblastoma cells during surgery and destroy microscopic cancer left behind afterward. In mice, the treatment prevented recurrence and led to 100% survival at 60 days, though it has not yet been tested in humans.

articles.title: Scientists discover a brain “brake” that can shut down chronic pain
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a brain-based “brake” that can shut down chronic nerve pain in mice by calming an overactive pain circuit. Targeting this system more precisely could one day lead to powerful pain relief without affecting opioid receptors throughout the entire body.
